source_findings.scope: Only CUDA_SRC and _ext AST nodes differ. Removing the exact hint/resource additions restores the parent CUDA byte for byte; namespace/verbosity normalization restores _ext. All41 other named Python nodes remain identical.
source_findings.future_target: The hint follows the current actual weight TMA and targets the third future item within the current phase. A-phase rotated order is preserved, future expert lookup is used, and the final three items/short/empty phase ranges issue no hints.
source_findings.data_lifetime: Targets are immutable prepared weight-bank bytes; routing metadata was published by the unchanged WS_JOIN. The hint introduces no shared destination or cross-phase readiness assumption.
source_findings.ordering: Real-copy source/destination/byte count, expected-tx arrivals, empty-slot waits, phase bits and slot progression are unchanged. Neither consumers nor producers rely on hint completion.
source_findings.math_and_dispatch: Weight encoding, scale reconstruction, MMA instruction sequence, all compute and finalizer code, scratch, PDL and Python state/dispatch stay exact247888. No rejected SC6 encoding is present.
source_findings.resource_gate: Bounded LPFR helper queries both exact BIG pointers after setting unchanged dynamic shared231168, using unchanged576 threads. API failures/occupancy<1 throw before attr success is cached. Register/local diagnostics are informative, not an automatic performance rejection.
source_findings.compile_support: The plain instruction is specified for sm90+ in PTX8.0 onward, with16-byte address/size alignment. Actual CUDA assembly acceptance still requires the official build.

proof_results.limits: Native execution of actual producer/split control flow and address expressions uses uint64 byte-address and CUDA-operation shims. It proves emitted requests, bounds and ordering in these finite cases; not CUDA compilation, hardware asynchrony, hint execution/effectiveness, cache behavior, GPU tensor correctness or speed. Full source restoration proves the arithmetic/packing and other device paths unchanged; no new MMA or lifecycle simulator is used.

coverage_limits: The native harness replaces global pointers with uint64 byte addresses and translates CUDA operations into event records; it does not execute CUDA or model hardware asynchrony/cache effects.

The jE[256] fixture and start65519 cases extend beyond actual FT64 JMAX88. They are supplemental integer/address stress, not legal routing workloads or proof of enlarged production array capacity. The adjacent author note explicitly qualifies the misleading fixture comment.

Other finite native cases exercise ordinary job boundaries, rotations, empty phases, short/tail ranges and three expert-ID patterns. The earlier independent plan arithmetic separately bounded real88-job addresses.
No claim of global-zero-job support follows from producer empty-range tests; inherited routing-stage behavior is unchanged.
Source restoration and identical emitted real-request traces do not predict compiled register allocation, achieved occupancy, hint effectiveness, DRAM traffic or latency.

accepted_performance_gate.required_official_evidence: Clean setup,5 tests,6 benchmarks,6 profiles with source/evaluator/case identity; actual valid resource admission; activation inferred only from pinned source/log/profile premises.
accepted_performance_gate.interpretation: Root accepted before implementation. Operational consistency screen, not statistical significance or permission to choose a better-looking subset after the result.

performance_risk: Almost one extra cache request per real weight stage plus future-address work can be ignored, contend with demand traffic or cause cache pollution. The fixed experiment is justified by its small isolated mechanism and information value, not by a measured stall or a speed forecast.
